title: CPX, MVV & Respiratory Muscle Strength Quiz

questions.text: Which statement best defines CPX, CPEX, or CPET?

answers.text: A test that measures only residual volume after maximal expiration
A test designed to assess ventilation, gas exchange, and cardiovascular function during exercise
A test that measures airway inflammation using exhaled nitric oxide
A test used only to collect resting arterial blood gases

questions.text: Which is an indication for CPX?

answers.text: PaO2 less than 40 mmHg on room air

questions.text: A patient has a PaCO2 greater than 70 mmHg. How is this classified for CPX in the lesson?
When choosing between treadmill and cycle ergometer for CPX, what dictates the choice?

answers.text: The availability of a Borg scale only

questions.text: Which CPX equipment is used to measure exhaled O2, CO2, and N2?
Which pre-procedure item is listed for CPX when hypoxemia is suspected?
Which patient instruction is part of CPX preparation?

answers.text: Smoke cigarettes up to 1 hour before the test
Avoid exercise the day of the test
Stop all medications unless told otherwise by the patient
Wear restrictive clothing to improve measurements

questions.text: Which description matches the maximal incremental cycle protocol?

answers.text: Six minutes of walking at the patient's own pace
3 minutes rest, 3 minutes unloaded cycling, then increasing watts every minute
Five breaths of solution followed by spirometry
Deep and rapid breathing for 12 seconds only

questions.text: Which finding is an indication to terminate CPX?

answers.text: Heart rate below predicted maximum at rest

questions.text: What does VO2 measure during CPX?

answers.text: The volume of O2 used by tissues each minute
Exhaled nitric oxide in parts per billion

questions.text: Which criterion can classify a CPX as maximal effort?
Which statement best defines MVV?

answers.text: Maximum volume a patient can breathe over a specified period, usually 12 seconds
Maximum positive pressure produced after a complete inhalation
Distance a patient can walk in 6 minutes
Oxygen used by tissues at each minute during exercise

questions.text: Which is an indication for MVV?

answers.text: To set a ventilatory limit during exercise

questions.text: Which hazard is common during MVV because of hyperventilation?

answers.text: Improved oxygen saturation in all patients

questions.text: During MVV, the patient's rate should generally be:
MVV is influenced by which factor?

answers.text: Condition of the ventilatory control mechanism

questions.text: What does MIP primarily reflect?

answers.text: Strength of the diaphragm and other inspiratory muscles
Strength of the abdominal and expiratory muscles only

questions.text: What does MEP primarily reflect?

answers.text: Strength of the abdominal and other expiratory muscles

questions.text: During MIP testing, which pressure should be recorded?

answers.text: The largest negative pressure sustained for at least 1 second
The first transient positive pressure spike
The lowest oxygen saturation during a walk test
The average FeNO value after spirometry

questions.text: Which pattern suggests inspiratory muscle weakness, usually diaphragmatic?

answers.text: Normal FeNO with high walk distance
